towns.name: Methuen
towns.rail: None in town — Lawrence, Bradford and Haverhill stations (Haverhill Line) nearby
towns.card: I-93 and I-495, Forest Lake, the Music Hall
towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Methuen, MA: the housing stock, I-93/I-495 and the nearby Haverhill Line, schools, local facts and live market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa.
towns.lede: On the New Hampshire line between Lawrence, Haverhill and Dracut — with I-93 and I-495 both running through it.
intro: Methuen sits on the New Hampshire border, wrapped around the north side of Lawrence, with Haverhill to the east and Dracut to the west. I-93 begins its Massachusetts run here and I-495 crosses the eastern side of the city, so for a lot of my clients it is the practical middle of the Merrimack Valley: quick to the highways, quick to Salem, NH, and a short drive to the Lawrence train station.
It has a mayor–council city government, though you will still hear plenty of people call it “the town.” My office is a few minutes away in Lawrence, and Methuen is one of the places I work most.
housing: Methuen’s housing is varied, which is a big part of its appeal. Closer to the Lawrence line and around the older center you will find two- and three-family homes and older single-families on smaller lots. Further out, mid-century capes, ranches and split-levels give way to colonials, newer subdivisions and condominium communities.

That range lets a buyer trade lot size against commute, and it gives investors owner-occupied multi-family options without leaving a suburban city. On older homes, we plan the inspection around heating systems, electrical, roofs and — for any home built before 1978 — lead paint.

ways.d: There is no station in Methuen. Most commuters drive to Lawrence station on the MBTA Haverhill Line, or to Bradford or Haverhill, for service to Boston’s North Station.
I-93 has exits in Methuen and I-495 crosses the east side of the city; Route 213, the Loop Connector, links the two. Routes 28, 110 and 113 handle local trips.
Salem and Pelham, New Hampshire, border Methuen to the north, so shopping and work in Southern New Hampshire are a short drive.

towns.schools: Methuen’s public schools are run by the Methuen Public School District. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: A concert hall built to house a large pipe organ, and one of the city’s best-known landmarks.
A recreational great pond of a little over 55 acres in the city.
The public library building was completed in 1883. The nearby Searles Tenney Nevins Historic District was established in 1992.
A small state park within the city.

faq: Is there a train from Methuen to Boston?
Not inside Methuen. Most people drive to Lawrence station on the MBTA Haverhill Line, or to Bradford or Haverhill, for service to North Station. Check the MBTA schedule for current times and parking.
What kinds of homes are in Methuen?
A wide mix: two- and three-family homes and older single-families near the Lawrence line and the older center, and capes, ranches, split-levels, colonials and condominiums further out.
Can my first home in Methuen be a two- or three-family?

Yes. If you live in one unit, owner-occupied financing such as FHA can be used on two- to four-unit homes, and part of the rent can help you qualify. My first multi-family guide walks through the numbers.

es.description: Vivir, comprar o vender en Methuen, MA: tipos de vivienda, I-93/I-495 y el tren en Lawrence, escuelas, datos locales y el mercado al día — con Eduardo Inoa, REALTOR® bilingüe.
es.lede: En la frontera con New Hampshire, entre Lawrence, Haverhill y Dracut — con la I-93 y la I-495 pasando por la ciudad.
intro: Methuen rodea el norte de Lawrence, con Haverhill al este, Dracut al oeste y New Hampshire justo arriba. La I-93 empieza su recorrido por Massachusetts aquí y la I-495 cruza el lado este de la ciudad. Por eso, para muchas de las familias con las que trabajo, Methuen es el punto práctico del Merrimack Valley: cerca de las autopistas, cerca de Salem, NH, y a pocos minutos de la estación de tren de Lawrence.
Tiene gobierno de ciudad, con alcalde y concejo, aunque mucha gente todavía le dice “el pueblo”. Mi oficina está a pocos minutos, en Lawrence, y Methuen es uno de los lugares donde más trabajo.
housing: En Methuen hay de todo, y eso es parte de su atractivo. Cerca de la línea con Lawrence y alrededor del centro viejo hay casas de dos y tres familias y casas unifamiliares antiguas en lotes más pequeños. Más hacia afuera encontrará capes, ranches y split-levels de mediados del siglo pasado, colonials, urbanizaciones más nuevas y condominios.

Esa variedad le permite escoger entre más terreno o un trayecto más corto, y le da al inversionista opciones de multifamiliares para vivir en una unidad sin salir de una ciudad tranquila. En las casas antiguas revisamos con cuidado la calefacción, la electricidad, el techo y — en toda casa construida antes de 1978 — la pintura con plomo.

ways.d: No hay estación en Methuen. La mayoría maneja hasta la estación de Lawrence, en la línea Haverhill del MBTA, o hasta Bradford o Haverhill, para llegar a North Station en Boston.
La I-93 tiene salidas en Methuen y la I-495 cruza el lado este de la ciudad; la Ruta 213 (el Loop Connector) une las dos. Las Rutas 28, 110 y 113 sirven para moverse dentro de la zona.

ways.t: Al otro lado de la frontera
ways.d: Salem y Pelham, New Hampshire, colindan con Methuen por el norte, así que las tiendas y los trabajos del sur de New Hampshire quedan muy cerca.

es.schools: Las escuelas públicas de Methuen dependen del Methuen Public School District. Para asignación de escuela, matrícula y programas, consulte directamente con el distrito — es la única fuente que yo recomiendo.

know.d: Una sala de conciertos construida para albergar un gran órgano de tubos; uno de los lugares más conocidos de la ciudad.
Un lago recreativo de poco más de 55 acres dentro de la ciudad.
El edificio de la biblioteca pública se terminó en 1883. El distrito histórico Searles Tenney Nevins se estableció en 1992.
Un pequeño parque estatal dentro de la ciudad.

faq: ¿Hay tren de Methuen a Boston?

Dentro de Methuen no. La mayoría maneja hasta la estación de Lawrence, en la línea Haverhill del MBTA, o hasta Bradford o Haverhill, para llegar a North Station. Revise el horario del MBTA para los horarios y el estacionamiento actuales.
¿Qué tipo de casas hay en Methuen?
Una mezcla amplia: casas de dos y tres familias y unifamiliares antiguas cerca de Lawrence y del centro viejo, y capes, ranches, split-levels, colonials y condominios más hacia afuera.
¿Mi primera casa en Methuen puede ser de dos o tres familias?

Sí. Si usted vive en una de las unidades, puede usar financiamiento para dueño-ocupante, como FHA, en casas de dos a cuatro unidades, y parte de la renta puede ayudarle a calificar. Se lo explico con números en una llamada de 20 minutos.

towns.name: Lawrence
towns.card: Mill city on the Merrimack, with its own train station
towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Lawrence, MA: triple-deckers and multi-families, the Haverhill Line station, schools, local history and live market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa, based in Lawrence.
towns.lede: A compact mill city on both banks of the Merrimack — and the home of my office.
intro: Lawrence is where I work from every day — our office is at 130 Parker St, Suite 14. The city was laid out in the 1840s as a planned industrial city, built around the Great Stone Dam and the canals that powered its mills on both banks of the Merrimack River.

What that history left behind is what buyers come for today: a commuter rail station with direct service to Boston, I-495 along the city’s edge, and a large stock of two-, three- and four-family homes that make owning — and renting out part of what you own — possible.
housing: Lawrence is a city of triple-deckers and two-families, many built in the late 1800s and early 1900s, along with brick mill-era buildings, single-families in the outer sections of the city and residential lofts in converted mill buildings near the river and canals.

For buyers who want to live in one unit and rent the others, Lawrence is often where we look first. Older buildings need a careful plan: heating systems, electrical, porches and egress, and lead paint — in Massachusetts, the owner must delead a unit when a child under six lives there. At sale, every home needs a smoke and carbon-monoxide certificate from the fire department.

ways.d: Lawrence station is on the MBTA Haverhill Line with service to Boston’s North Station; Andover is the next stop south and Bradford the next stop north.
I-495 runs along the city with several exits, Routes 28 and 114 cross the city, and I-93 is a short drive west through Methuen or Andover.
The Merrimack Valley Regional Transit Authority (MVRTA) runs local bus routes through Lawrence and the surrounding towns.

towns.schools: Lawrence’s public schools are run by Lawrence Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment, bilingual programs and registration, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: Built across the Merrimack in the 1840s to power the mills; when it was finished it was described as the largest dam in the world.
The textile strike that began in Lawrence’s mills in 1912 is one of the most widely studied labor struggles in American history.
A state park that tells the story of the mill city, near the canals downtown.
The community was set off as a town in 1847 and became a city in 1853.

faq: Is there a train from Lawrence to Boston?
Yes. Lawrence station is on the MBTA Haverhill Line with service to North Station. Check the MBTA schedule for current times and parking.
Can I buy a two- or three-family in Lawrence as my first home?

Yes. If you live in one unit, owner-occupied financing such as FHA can be used on two- to four-unit homes, and part of the rent can help you qualify. My first multi-family guide covers the numbers lenders look at.
What should I check before buying an older multi-family in Lawrence?

Heating, electrical, roof, porches and exits, and the lead paint status of each unit. Massachusetts requires an owner to delead a unit when a child under six lives there, and every sale needs a smoke and carbon-monoxide certificate. I build those into the offer and inspection plan from day one.

es.description: Vivir, comprar o vender en Lawrence, MA: casas de dos y tres familias, el tren a Boston, escuelas, historia y el mercado al día — con Eduardo Inoa, REALTOR® bilingüe con oficina en Lawrence.
es.lede: Una ciudad de molinos a ambos lados del río Merrimack — y donde está mi oficina.
intro: Lawrence es mi casa de trabajo — nuestra oficina está en 130 Parker St, Suite 14. La ciudad se diseñó en los años 1840 como ciudad industrial, alrededor de la Great Stone Dam y de los canales que movían los molinos a ambos lados del río Merrimack.

Esa historia dejó justo lo que muchos compradores buscan hoy: una estación de tren con servicio directo a Boston, la I-495 al lado de la ciudad y muchísimas casas de dos, tres y cuatro familias, que hacen posible comprar y que parte de la renta le ayude a pagar la hipoteca.
housing: Lawrence es una ciudad de triple-deckers y casas de dos familias, muchas construidas entre finales del 1800 y principios del 1900, además de edificios de ladrillo de la época de los molinos, casas unifamiliares en las zonas más afueras y lofts en molinos convertidos cerca del río y los canales.

Si usted quiere vivir en una unidad y alquilar las otras, Lawrence suele ser el primer lugar donde buscamos. Los edificios antiguos piden un buen plan: calefacción, electricidad, balcones y salidas, y la pintura con plomo — en Massachusetts, el dueño tiene que hacer el desleading de una unidad cuando vive allí un niño menor de seis años. Y al vender, toda casa necesita el certificado de detectores de humo y monóxido de carbono del departamento de bomberos.

ways.d: La estación de Lawrence está en la línea Haverhill del MBTA, con servicio a North Station en Boston; Andover es la próxima parada hacia el sur y Bradford hacia el norte.
La I-495 pasa por la ciudad con varias salidas, las Rutas 28 y 114 la cruzan, y la I-93 queda a pocos minutos al oeste, por Methuen o Andover.
La Merrimack Valley Regional Transit Authority (MVRTA) tiene rutas de autobús locales en Lawrence y los pueblos de alrededor.

es.schools: Las escuelas públicas de Lawrence dependen de Lawrence Public Schools. Para asignación de escuela, matrícula, programas bilingües e inscripción, consulte directamente con el distrito — es la única fuente que yo recomiendo.

know.d: Se construyó sobre el Merrimack en los años 1840 para darle fuerza a los molinos; cuando se terminó, se describía como la represa más grande del mundo.
La huelga textil que empezó en los molinos de Lawrence en 1912 es una de las luchas obreras más estudiadas de la historia de Estados Unidos.
Un parque estatal que cuenta la historia de la ciudad de los molinos, cerca de los canales del centro.

know.t: Lleva el nombre de Abbott Lawrence
know.d: Se estableció como pueblo en 1847 y se convirtió en ciudad en 1853.

faq: ¿Hay tren de Lawrence a Boston?
Sí. La estación de Lawrence está en la línea Haverhill del MBTA, con servicio a North Station. Revise el horario del MBTA para los horarios y el estacionamiento actuales.
¿Puedo comprar una casa de dos o tres familias en Lawrence como mi primera casa?

Sí. Si usted vive en una de las unidades, puede usar financiamiento para dueño-ocupante, como FHA, en casas de dos a cuatro unidades, y parte de la renta puede ayudarle a calificar. Le explico los números que mira el banco en una llamada de 20 minutos.
¿Qué debo revisar antes de comprar un multifamiliar antiguo en Lawrence?

La calefacción, la electricidad, el techo, los balcones y las salidas, y la situación del plomo en cada unidad. En Massachusetts, el dueño tiene que hacer el desleading cuando vive allí un niño menor de seis años, y toda venta necesita el certificado de detectores de humo y monóxido de carbono. Eso lo incluyo en la oferta y en el plan de inspección desde el primer día.

towns.name: Haverhill
towns.incorporated: Founded 1640; Bradford joined the city in 1897
towns.rail: Haverhill and Bradford stations, MBTA Haverhill Line
towns.card: Two train stations, a riverfront downtown, room to spread out
towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Haverhill, MA: multi-families, shoe-factory lofts and larger lots, two Haverhill Line stations, schools, local facts and live market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa.
towns.lede: On the Merrimack at the end of the train line that carries its name — with the New Hampshire border along its northern edge.
intro: Haverhill sits on the Merrimack River at the end of the MBTA line that carries its name, with the New Hampshire border along its northern edge. It has two commuter rail stations — Haverhill and Bradford — a downtown of brick buildings from its shoe-making years, and quieter, more open roads toward its outer edges.
Bradford, across the river from downtown, was its own town until it joined Haverhill in 1897. Between the two sides you get a wide spread of homes, prices and lot sizes inside one city.
housing: Downtown and the older neighborhoods around it have two- and three-family homes, Victorians, and residential lofts in converted shoe-factory buildings. Bradford mixes older homes with mid-century streets. Further out you will find colonials, capes and newer subdivisions on larger lots, and some farm properties.

For owner-occupant investors, Haverhill’s multi-families sit within reach of a train station; for buyers who want space, the outer sections offer it without leaving Massachusetts. On older homes we plan around heating, electrical, roofs and lead paint for anything built before 1978.

ways.d: Haverhill is the outer end of the MBTA Haverhill Line, and Bradford is the stop just before it — both with service to Boston’s North Station.
I-495 has several exits in the city. Routes 97, 108, 110, 113 and 125 handle local trips and connections to New Hampshire.
Salem, Atkinson and Plaistow, New Hampshire, border Haverhill to the north.

towns.schools: Haverhill’s public schools are run by Haverhill Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: Haverhill was a shoe-making center; by the end of 1913, about one in ten shoes made in the United States came from the city.
Built in 1875 as a residence, it stands in the Winnekenni Park Conservation Area.
The poet was from Haverhill, and his best-known poem, “Snow-Bound,” is set there.
A separate town until January 1, 1897, when it became part of Haverhill.

faq: Is there a train from Haverhill to Boston?
Yes, two stations: Haverhill, at the outer end of the MBTA Haverhill Line, and Bradford. Both have service to North Station. Check the MBTA schedule for current times and parking.
What kinds of homes are in Haverhill?

Two- and three-family homes, Victorians and converted shoe-factory lofts near downtown; older and mid-century homes in Bradford; colonials, capes, newer subdivisions and some farm properties further out.
Is Haverhill close to New Hampshire?
Yes. Salem, Atkinson and Plaistow, New Hampshire, border the city to the north, and I am licensed in both states, so we can compare homes on either side of the line.

es.lede: Sobre el Merrimack, al final de la línea de tren que lleva su nombre — con New Hampshire justo al norte.
intro: Haverhill está sobre el río Merrimack, al final de la línea del MBTA que lleva su nombre, con la frontera de New Hampshire al norte. Tiene dos estaciones de tren — Haverhill y Bradford —, un centro de edificios de ladrillo de la época de las fábricas de zapatos y, hacia las afueras, calles más tranquilas y con más terreno.
Bradford, al otro lado del río, era un pueblo aparte hasta que se unió a Haverhill en 1897. Entre los dos lados hay una gran variedad de casas, precios y tamaños de lote dentro de una misma ciudad.
housing: En el centro y los vecindarios viejos alrededor hay casas de dos y tres familias, casas victorianas y lofts en antiguas fábricas de zapatos. Bradford combina casas antiguas con calles de mediados del siglo pasado. Más hacia afuera hay colonials, capes y urbanizaciones nuevas en lotes más grandes, y algunas fincas.

Para el que quiere vivir en una unidad y alquilar las demás, los multifamiliares de Haverhill quedan cerca de una estación de tren; para el que busca espacio, las afueras lo ofrecen sin salir de Massachusetts. En las casas antiguas revisamos la calefacción, la electricidad, el techo y el plomo en todo lo construido antes de 1978.

ways.d: Haverhill es la última parada de la línea Haverhill del MBTA, y Bradford es la anterior — las dos con servicio a North Station en Boston.
La I-495 tiene varias salidas en la ciudad. Las Rutas 97, 108, 110, 113 y 125 sirven para moverse dentro de la zona y hacia New Hampshire.

ways.d: Salem, Atkinson y Plaistow, New Hampshire, colindan con Haverhill por el norte.

es.schools: Las escuelas públicas de Haverhill dependen de Haverhill Public Schools. Para asignación de escuela, matrícula y programas, consulte directamente con el distrito — es la única fuente que yo recomiendo.

know.d: Haverhill fue un centro del calzado; a finales de 1913, cerca de uno de cada diez zapatos hechos en Estados Unidos salía de la ciudad.
Se construyó en 1875 como residencia y está dentro del área de conservación del Winnekenni Park.
El poeta era de Haverhill, y su poema más conocido, “Snow-Bound”, transcurre allí.
Fue un pueblo aparte hasta el 1 de enero de 1897, cuando pasó a formar parte de Haverhill.

faq: ¿Hay tren de Haverhill a Boston?

Casas de dos y tres familias, victorianas y lofts en antiguas fábricas cerca del centro; casas antiguas y de mediados del siglo pasado en Bradford; y colonials, capes, urbanizaciones nuevas y algunas fincas más hacia afuera.
¿Haverhill queda cerca de New Hampshire?
Sí. Salem, Atkinson y Plaistow, New Hampshire, colindan con la ciudad por el norte, y yo tengo licencia en los dos estados, así que podemos comparar casas a ambos lados de la frontera.

towns.name: Andover
towns.rail: Andover and Ballardvale stations, MBTA Haverhill Line
towns.roads: I-93 and I-495 (they meet in town), Routes 28, 125 and 133
towns.card: Two train stations and the I-93/I-495 interchange
towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Andover, MA: colonials and historic homes, two Haverhill Line stations, the I-93/I-495 interchange, schools and live market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa.
towns.lede: A classic New England town just south of Lawrence, with two train stations and the I-93/I-495 interchange inside its borders.
intro: Andover sits just south of Lawrence, with a traditional downtown along Main Street, two commuter rail stations and the interchange of I-93 and I-495 inside the town. Few places in the region combine rail, both interstates and a classic town center so closely.
It is one of the oldest towns in the area — incorporated in 1646 — and that shows in its historic centers, from the village around Main Street to Shawsheen Village and Ballardvale.
housing: Andover is mostly single-family. Colonials from many decades dominate, from historic homes near the center, in Shawsheen Village and in Ballardvale, to larger contemporary colonials on bigger lots in the outer parts of town. There are also condominium and townhouse communities and a smaller number of two-families.

Because so much of the stock is single-family on established lots, buyers here usually weigh age and condition against lot and location. On historic homes, ask the town early whether any local preservation rules apply before planning exterior changes.

ways.d: Andover has two stops on the MBTA Haverhill Line — Andover and Ballardvale — with service to Boston’s North Station.
I-93 and I-495 meet in Andover. Route 28 is the main north–south road through town, and Routes 125 and 133 also cross it.
Lawrence, North Andover and Tewksbury are next door, and the Lawrence station is one stop north.

towns.schools: Andover’s public schools are run by Andover Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: The independent boarding school was founded in Andover in 1778.
A planned mill community; its mill was announced in 1919 and began operating in 1922.
A state forest on the border of Andover, Middleton and North Reading.
One of the oldest towns in the Merrimack Valley; North Andover was part of it until 1855.

faq: Does Andover have commuter rail?
Yes, two stations on the MBTA Haverhill Line: Andover and Ballardvale, both with service to North Station. Check the MBTA schedule for current times and parking.
What kinds of homes are in Andover?
Mostly single-family colonials, from historic homes near the center and in Shawsheen Village and Ballardvale to newer colonials on larger lots, plus condominium and townhouse communities.
How close is Andover to the interstates?
Very close: I-93 and I-495 meet inside the town, and Route 28 runs north–south through it.

towns.name: North Andover
towns.rail: None in town — Lawrence station (Haverhill Line) is closest
towns.card: The Old Center, Lake Cochichewick, Route 114
towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in North Andover, MA: colonials, antiques and larger lots, I-495 and Route 114, the nearby Lawrence station, schools and live market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa.
towns.lede: A town of its own since 1855 — with a historic Old Center, Lake Cochichewick and quick access to I-495.
intro: North Andover separated from Andover in 1855 and has its own distinct shape: a historic Old Center near the geographic middle of town, Lake Cochichewick across the north-east, Merrimack College, and I-495 along the Lawrence border.
For buyers it is a town of single-family homes on established lots, a short drive from the Lawrence train station and from the stores and services of Route 114.
housing: North Andover is mostly single-family: antique homes around the Old Center, capes and ranches from the middle of the last century, colonials of many ages, and newer subdivisions with larger lots. There are also condominium and townhouse communities.

Lots tend to be larger than in the cities next door, and some homes use a private septic system instead of town sewer — something we confirm on every home before an offer, because Massachusetts generally requires a Title 5 septic inspection when a home with a septic system is sold.

ways.d: There is no station in North Andover. The closest is Lawrence station on the MBTA Haverhill Line; Andover station is also nearby.
I-495 crosses the western part of town along the Lawrence border. Route 114, the Salem Turnpike, runs through town, and Routes 125 and 133 share much of their path here.
Lawrence, Andover, Methuen and Haverhill are next door, with Boxford and Middleton to the east and south.

towns.schools: North Andover’s public schools are run by North Andover Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: North Andover’s historic Old Center, near the middle of town, hosts many town events.
The lake takes up much of the north-east quarter of town.
A Catholic, Augustinian four-year college located in the town.
Weir Hill has trails with views over the area, and Harold Parker State Forest nearby offers trails, a campground and a freshwater swimming beach.

faq: Is there a train station in North Andover?
No. Most commuters use Lawrence station, a short drive away on the MBTA Haverhill Line, or Andover station.
What kinds of homes are in North Andover?
Mostly single-family: antiques around the Old Center, mid-century capes and ranches, colonials of many ages, newer subdivisions on larger lots, and some condominium and townhouse communities.
Do homes in North Andover have septic systems?

Some do, especially in the outer parts of town. When a home has a septic system, Massachusetts generally requires a Title 5 inspection at sale, so we confirm sewer or septic on every home before making an offer.

towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Dracut, MA: single-families, open space and newer subdivisions, Routes 38/110/113 and nearby Lowell station, schools and live market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa.
towns.lede: Across the Merrimack from Lowell, running north to the New Hampshire line — with open land still in the mix.
intro: Dracut sits across the Merrimack River from Lowell and runs north to Pelham, New Hampshire, with Methuen to the east and Tyngsborough to the west. It was settled as a farming and mill community, and some of those rural landscapes are still intact alongside newer neighborhoods.
It is also one of the largest towns in Massachusetts still governed by an open town meeting. For buyers, the draw is a suburban town within a short drive of Lowell’s train station, I-93 and I-495.
housing: Most of Dracut is single-family: capes, ranches and colonials from the post-war decades, newer subdivisions, and condominium communities, with some two-families in the sections closest to Lowell and a few remaining farm properties.

Many homes in town are on public sewer and some are on septic. We confirm which before an offer, because Massachusetts generally requires a Title 5 inspection when a home with a septic system is sold.

ways.d: There is no station in Dracut. Lowell station, the end of the MBTA Lowell Line, is closest, and the LRTA 10 bus connects to it.
Routes 38, 110 and 113 run directly through town. I-93 is reached through Methuen, and I-495 and Route 3 through Lowell.
Pelham, New Hampshire, borders Dracut to the north.

One of the largest towns in Massachusetts still run by an open town meeting.
The brook runs through the middle of town on its way to the Merrimack.
The Lowell–Dracut–Tyngsboro State Forest extends into the town.

faq: Is there a train from Dracut to Boston?

Mostly single-family capes, ranches and colonials, newer subdivisions and condominium communities, with some two-families near Lowell and a few farm properties.
Are homes in Dracut on sewer or septic?

intro: Tewksbury’s biggest asset is access. I-93 and I-495 both run through town, Lowell is next door, and Boston is about 19 miles away. The Merrimack River forms part of its northern boundary and the Shawsheen River runs through its southern end.
For buyers commuting by car in almost any direction — Boston, the 495 belt or Southern New Hampshire — it is one of the most convenient towns in the area.

I-93 and I-495 both pass through town, and Route 38 is the main local road.
Lowell, Dracut, Andover, Wilmington and Billerica border the town.

towns.schools: Tewksbury’s public schools are run by Tewksbury Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

The Merrimack forms part of the northern boundary and the Shawsheen runs through the south end of town.

towns.name: Lowell
towns.rail: Lowell station, end of the MBTA Lowell Line
towns.roads: I-495, Route 3, the Lowell Connector, Routes 38, 110 and 113
towns.card: Canals, mills, a national park and its own rail line
towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Lowell, MA: triple-deckers, Victorians and mill lofts, the Lowell Line to Boston, schools, local history and live market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa.
towns.lede: The mill city at full scale — where the Merrimack and Concord rivers meet, and where the Lowell Line begins.
intro: Lowell was built at the meeting of the Merrimack and Concord rivers as a planned mill town, and its canals still run through downtown. Today it is home to Lowell National Historical Park, UMass Lowell and the outer end of the MBTA Lowell Line, with I-495 and Route 3 linked by the Lowell Connector.
For buyers, that adds up to a city with real transit, a deep stock of multi-family homes and a wide range of housing from downtown lofts to single-families in the outer neighborhoods.
housing: Lowell has triple-deckers and two-families throughout its older neighborhoods, Victorians on its hillside streets, and loft condominiums and apartments in converted mill buildings downtown. The outer neighborhoods add capes, ranches and colonials.

For house-hackers, Lowell is one of the main places in the region to buy a two- to four-family and live in one unit. Older buildings need a careful plan: heating, electrical, porches and egress, and lead paint — Massachusetts requires an owner to delead a unit when a child under six lives there.

ways.d: Lowell station, at Gallagher Terminal, is the outer end of the MBTA Lowell Line, about 25 miles from Boston’s North Station.
I-495 and Route 3 both serve the city, joined by the Lowell Connector. Routes 38, 110 and 113 handle local trips.
The Lowell Regional Transit Authority (LRTA) runs bus routes connecting Lowell with the surrounding towns.

towns.schools: Lowell’s public schools are run by Lowell Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment, language programs and registration, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: Established in the late 1970s, it includes about 5.6 miles of restored canals and the mill buildings that made Lowell.
The city sits where the Concord River meets the Merrimack, near the mile-long rapids of Pawtucket Falls.
The state university has its campuses in the city.
The writer was born in Lowell, in the Centralville neighborhood.

faq: Is there a train from Lowell to Boston?
Yes. Lowell station is the outer end of the MBTA Lowell Line, with service to North Station. Check the MBTA schedule for current times and parking.
Can I buy a two- or three-family in Lowell as my first home?

Yes. If you live in one unit, owner-occupied financing such as FHA can be used on two- to four-unit homes, and part of the rent can help you qualify. My first multi-family guide covers the numbers lenders look at.
What kinds of homes are in Lowell?
Triple-deckers and two-families, Victorians, loft condominiums in converted mills downtown, and capes, ranches and colonials in the outer neighborhoods.

es.rail: Estación de Lowell, última parada de la línea Lowell del MBTA
es.roads: I-495, Ruta 3, el Lowell Connector, Rutas 38, 110 y 113
es.card: Canales, molinos, un parque nacional y su propia línea de tren
es.description: Vivir, comprar o vender en Lowell, MA: triple-deckers, casas victorianas y lofts en molinos, el tren a Boston, escuelas, historia y el mercado al día — con Eduardo Inoa, REALTOR® bilingüe.
es.lede: La ciudad de los molinos en grande — donde se unen los ríos Merrimack y Concord, y donde empieza la línea Lowell.
intro: Lowell se construyó donde se unen los ríos Merrimack y Concord, como ciudad de molinos planificada, y sus canales todavía cruzan el centro. Hoy tiene el Lowell National Historical Park, la universidad UMass Lowell y la última parada de la línea Lowell del MBTA, con la I-495 y la Ruta 3 unidas por el Lowell Connector.

Para el comprador, eso significa una ciudad con transporte de verdad, muchísimas casas multifamiliares y opciones que van desde lofts en el centro hasta casas unifamiliares en los vecindarios de afuera.
housing: Lowell tiene triple-deckers y casas de dos familias en todos sus vecindarios viejos, casas victorianas en las calles de las lomas y lofts — condominios y apartamentos — en molinos convertidos del centro. Los vecindarios de afuera suman capes, ranches y colonials.

Si usted quiere comprar de dos a cuatro unidades y vivir en una, Lowell es uno de los lugares principales de la región. Los edificios antiguos piden un buen plan: calefacción, electricidad, balcones y salidas, y la pintura con plomo — en Massachusetts, el dueño tiene que hacer el desleading de una unidad cuando vive allí un niño menor de seis años.

ways.d: La estación de Lowell, en el Gallagher Terminal, es la última parada de la línea Lowell del MBTA, a unas 25 millas de North Station en Boston.
La I-495 y la Ruta 3 pasan por la ciudad, unidas por el Lowell Connector. Las Rutas 38, 110 y 113 sirven para moverse dentro de la zona.
La Lowell Regional Transit Authority (LRTA) tiene rutas de autobús entre Lowell y los pueblos de alrededor.

es.schools: Las escuelas públicas de Lowell dependen de Lowell Public Schools. Para asignación de escuela, matrícula, programas de idiomas e inscripción, consulte directamente con el distrito — es la única fuente que yo recomiendo.

know.d: Creado a finales de los años 70, incluye unas 5.6 millas de canales restaurados y los molinos que hicieron a Lowell.
La ciudad está donde el río Concord se une al Merrimack, cerca de los rápidos de Pawtucket Falls.
La universidad estatal tiene sus recintos en la ciudad.
El escritor nació en Lowell, en el vecindario de Centralville.

faq: ¿Hay tren de Lowell a Boston?
Sí. La estación de Lowell es la última parada de la línea Lowell del MBTA, con servicio a North Station. Revise el horario del MBTA para los horarios y el estacionamiento actuales.
¿Puedo comprar una casa de dos o tres familias en Lowell como mi primera casa?

Sí. Si usted vive en una de las unidades, puede usar financiamiento para dueño-ocupante, como FHA, en casas de dos a cuatro unidades, y parte de la renta puede ayudarle a calificar. Le explico los números que mira el banco en una llamada de 20 minutos.
¿Qué tipo de casas hay en Lowell?
Triple-deckers y casas de dos familias, victorianas, lofts en molinos convertidos del centro, y capes, ranches y colonials en los vecindarios de afuera.

intro: Tyngsborough sits on the Route 3 corridor between Lowell and Nashua, New Hampshire. The Merrimack River runs through town, crossed by the Tyngsborough Bridge, and the town borders Nashua, Hudson and Pelham to the north.
For buyers who work along Route 3 — in Massachusetts or Southern New Hampshire — it is a town where the drive is the selling point.
housing: Tyngsborough is mostly single-family: capes, ranches and colonials, many on wooded lots, plus newer homes and condominium communities.

Some homes here use private septic systems or private wells, so we confirm both before an offer. Massachusetts generally requires a Title 5 septic inspection when a home with a septic system is sold, and a water test is worth doing on any private well.

ways.d: There is no station in Tyngsborough. Lowell station, the end of the MBTA Lowell Line, is closest; the LRTA 10 bus links eastern Tyngsborough to it.
Route 3 runs through town, toward Lowell and I-495 to the south and Nashua to the north.
Nashua, Hudson and Pelham, New Hampshire, border the town to the north.

The Lowell–Dracut–Tyngsboro State Forest extends into the town.

faq: Is there a train from Tyngsborough to Boston?

Mostly single-family capes, ranches and colonials, many on wooded lots, plus newer homes and condominium communities.

towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Chelmsford, MA: colonials, capes and village homes, the I-495/Route 3 junction, the Bruce Freeman Rail Trail, schools and county market data — from bilingual REALTOR® Eduardo Inoa.

It is a town of villages — Chelmsford Center, North Chelmsford, South, East and West Chelmsford and the Westlands — with the Bruce Freeman Rail Trail running through the center.
housing: Chelmsford is mostly single-family: colonials, capes, ranches and split-levels, with antique homes around the historic center and older village housing, including some multi-families, in North Chelmsford. There are also condominium and townhouse communities.
Because the stock is mostly established single-family, the usual trade-offs are age and condition against lot and location. We confirm sewer or septic on every home before an offer.

ways.d: There is no station in Chelmsford. LRTA bus routes connect the town to Lowell station on the MBTA Lowell Line, and North Billerica station is nearby.
I-495 and Route 3 meet in town. Routes 3A, 4, 27, 40, 110 and 129 also run through Chelmsford.
The Bruce Freeman Rail Trail runs through Chelmsford Center on its way south through Westford and beyond.

towns.schools: Chelmsford’s public schools are run by Chelmsford Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: The first section, through Lowell, Chelmsford and Westford, opened in 2009; the trail is named for a Chelmsford state legislator.
A house from 1691, now a museum.
The early-1800s canal ran through the town; its history is part of the local heritage.
Chelmsford was settled in 1652 and incorporated three years later.

faq: Is there a train station in Chelmsford?

Mostly single-family colonials, capes, ranches and split-levels, antique homes around the center, some older multi-families in North Chelmsford, and condominium and townhouse communities.

It is at the junction of I-495 and Route 3, so trips toward Boston, Nashua and the 495 belt start right in town.

The town is made up of distinct areas — Westford Center, Forge Village, Graniteville, Nabnasset and Parker Village — and historically produced granite, apples and worsted yarn.
housing: Westford is mostly single-family, with many colonials on larger lots, antique homes around the town center and the historic villages, and some condominium and townhouse communities.

Larger lots often come with private septic systems and, in places, private wells. We confirm both before an offer — Massachusetts generally requires a Title 5 septic inspection when a home with a septic system is sold.

ways.d: There is no station in Westford. The LRTA 15 bus runs along Route 110 to Chelmsford and Lowell station on the MBTA Lowell Line.
I-495 passes through town. Route 3 runs just to the east, with interchanges in Chelmsford and Tyngsborough, and Routes 27, 40, 110 and 225 serve the town.

towns.schools: Westford’s public schools are run by Westford Public Schools. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

towns.rail: No passenger rail — the closest stations are across the line in Massachusetts
towns.card: First stop on I-93 in New Hampshire
towns.description: Living in, buying or selling a home in Salem, NH: housing stock, I-93 and Route 28, New Hampshire taxes explained carefully, schools and live market data — from Eduardo Inoa, REALTOR® licensed in NH and MA.
towns.lede: The first New Hampshire town on I-93, right on the line with Methuen and Haverhill.
intro: Salem is the first New Hampshire town you reach on I-93, with Methuen and Haverhill on its southern border. It is known for retail along Route 28, the Mall at Rockingham Park and Tuscan Village, built on the site of the former Rockingham Park race track.

Because it is right on the state line, many of my clients compare Salem directly with Methuen, Haverhill and the other Merrimack Valley towns. I am licensed in both states, so we can do that side by side.
housing: Salem is mostly single-family: capes, ranches, split-levels and colonials, homes near Canobie Lake and the town’s other ponds, newer construction, and condominium communities.

Taxes are the other half of the housing picture. New Hampshire has no general sales tax and no state income tax on wages, and its tax on interest and dividends was repealed for tax periods beginning in 2025. The state relies more on local property taxes, so expect a higher property-tax rate than in many nearby Massachusetts towns — compare the actual tax bill on any home you consider. If you work in Massachusetts, Massachusetts generally taxes the wages you earn there; a tax professional can tell you what applies to you.

ways.d: I-93 runs through town with its first New Hampshire exits. NH Routes 28, 38, 97 and 111 handle local trips.
There is no passenger rail in Salem. The nearest commuter rail stations are in Massachusetts — Lawrence, Bradford and Haverhill on the MBTA Haverhill Line.
Methuen and Haverhill, Massachusetts, border Salem to the south; Windham, Pelham, Derry and Atkinson are its New Hampshire neighbors.

towns.schools: Salem’s public schools are run by the Salem School District. For school assignments, enrollment and programs, go straight to the district — it is the only source I point clients to.

know.d: A large amusement park on Canobie Lake.
A stone site of disputed origins in the town.
A mixed-use development on the site of the former Rockingham Park race track.
The town was incorporated under colonial governor Benning Wentworth.

faq: Does New Hampshire have a sales tax or income tax?

New Hampshire has no general sales tax and no state income tax on wages, and its interest-and-dividends tax was repealed for tax periods beginning in 2025. Property-tax rates are generally higher than in many nearby Massachusetts towns, so always compare the actual tax bill. If you work in Massachusetts, ask a tax professional how your wages are taxed.
Is there a train from Salem, NH, to Boston?
Not in Salem. The nearest commuter rail stations are in Massachusetts: Lawrence, Bradford and Haverhill on the MBTA Haverhill Line.
Can you help me sell in Massachusetts and buy in Salem?
Yes. I am licensed in both states, and I plan both closings together so you move once.
